thresholds.source: Hackathon Dossier v1.0, section 5.8 (teaching thresholds; values marked 'proposal' are not yet agreed with the partners)

gates.name: mrs_snr
gates.definition: SNR = height of the NAA peak in the real (absorption) spectrum, 1.9-2.1 ppm, divided by the SD of the real spectrum in the signal-free window -3.0 to 0.0 ppm (peak height / noise SD; LCModel's S/N uses 2 x RMS residual and gives about half)

gates.name: roi_u_consistency
gates.rule: for a mask propagated through a registration: stated_u_rel >= implied_u_rel = 3 * registration_rms_mm / r_eq, r_eq = equivalent-sphere radius of the reference ROI (dossier section 3.10)

gates.name: protocol_match
gates.rule: same sequence family, TE, TR and field as the baseline

twin_policy.note: R_factor is a declared team policy, not a physical constant (dossier section 7.5)

measurement.name: Choline-to-creatine ratio
measurement.physical_meaning: Ratio of two peak areas in a ¹H spectrum of one 20 mm cube of frontal tissue: choline (3.20 ppm, cell-membrane turnover) over creatine (3.03 ppm, energy metabolism, assumed stable).
measurement.how_measured: PRESS single-voxel spectroscopy, TE 30 ms, TR 2 s, 64 averages, 123.25 MHz (B0 = 2.895 T; label 3 T).
chain: ¹H spins precess at 123.25 MHz (MEASURED: FID)
Lorentzian fit of Cho and Cr peaks → amplitudes (DERIVED)
Twin belief about the metabolic state (INFERRED)
measurement.why_a_ratio: Coil sensitivity and voxel size cancel in a ratio; linewidth, relaxation and tissue mix do not.
measurement.spatial_support: VOI centre (-16, 45, 6) mm RAS, 20 × 20 × 20 mm; Cho and NAA voxels offset by 2.4 mm (chemical-shift displacement).
cannot_tell: absolute concentrations (needs a water reference and tissue correction)
a diagnosis (this is synthetic teaching data)
failure_modes: broad lines make Cho and Cr overlap (only ~21 Hz apart)
measurement.validation: Synthetic spectra with known amplitudes (StarterPack v0.3 FIDs).
measurement.epistemic: FID MEASURED-level (origin SIMULATED here); ratio DERIVED; twin state INFERRED

budget.rule: u_c = sqrt(sum of u_i^2) for independent sources (GUM)
budget.lesson: The fit term carries ~60 % of the variance, so the cheapest improvement is to re-shim and repeat.

canvas.title: Challenge canvas: Larmor, an evidence-gated health twin

intro.text: Team: Rehmoz Ayub, Ege Eroglu, Oussama Turki. Lane A (true change or measurement change?) joined with lane E (what measurement next?). Educational prototype on SIMULATED data. Not a clinical statement, not a diagnosis, not a medical device.

rows: One synthetic brain (subject `sub-01`), seen through one 20 mm cube of frontal tissue. The same scanner measures it twice, six months apart.
Single-voxel proton spectroscopy (1H MRS, PRESS, TE 30 ms, TR 2 s, 64 averages, 123.25 MHz) plus a T1-weighted MRI for the region volume.
Cho/Cr: the choline peak (3.20 ppm) divided by the creatine peak (3.03 ppm) in that voxel. NAA/Cr and the region volume ride along as secondary variables.
Cho/Cr went from 0.69 to 0.85. Did the tissue change, or did the measurement change? The second scan had broader lines (8.7 to 11.4 Hz) and less signal over noise (SNR 31 to 25).

A gated twin update with its reasons: Cho/Cr 0.69 becomes 0.741 ± 0.048 (update with warning, gain K = 0.32), a predicted range for a clean repeat (0.61 to 0.88), and one next measurement (re-shim and repeat, about 4 minutes).
Synthetic data, one subject, two sessions. The natural drift we allow for (process noise Q) is a teaching assumption, not a measured test-retest value.

blocks.text: We follow one synthetic brain, seen through one frontal voxel, across two spectroscopy sessions six months apart. The twin keeps a belief about Cho/Cr: a best value and how unsure it is. The follow-up value rose from 0.69 to 0.85, but the follow-up scan was worse. We want the twin to decide how much of that rise it may believe, show why, and say which measurement would settle the question for the least scanner time. The limit: the data are synthetic, so the result says nothing about any real person.

We named Cho/Cr as the primary variable before we looked at the follow-up numbers. Testing three variables and reporting whichever one moves is the multiple-testing trap (dossier section 3.10). So the rules are fixed in `nmr_twin/config.py`:

items: Primary variable: Cho/Cr. A change counts as significant when the absolute z is above 1.96 (two-sided 5 %).
Secondary variables (NAA/Cr, region volume): stricter limit, absolute z above 2.394 (Bonferroni, 0.05 divided by 3).
Model surprise: d² above 3.841 (chi-square, one degree of freedom, 95 %) raises a "model disagreement" flag.

blocks.text: We call the prototype a success when all of these hold. Each one is checked by an automatic test.

items: The baseline-to-follow-up update reproduces the dossier's worked example: z = 2.05, d² = 3.66, K = 0.32, posterior 0.741 ± 0.048.
Every twin number traces back to its source file, and the file's SHA-256 fingerprint is verified live.
All 20 practice packets (19 of ours plus the organizers' bad packet) get the expected decision: update, update with warning, or reject.
The twin names one next measurement, with its cost in scanner minutes and the uncertainty it removes.
The scientific claim stays modest: "suggestive, not conclusive". z = 2.05 is just above 1.96, and d² = 3.66 is just below 3.84.

blocks.text: We claim level 5 on the dossier's ladder (section 7.11), and one step past it.

items: Level 3, dynamic twin: a saved belief with its uncertainty, updated only by checked evidence.
Level 4, predictive: the twin states the range a clean repeat should fall in (0.61 to 0.88).

Level 5, evidence-steering: the twin ranks the next measurements and names the one that separates the explanations. When that repeat arrives (practice packet U01), the open question closes and the advice changes.
Past the ladder: we grade the twin against known truth. 250 simulated follow-ups with a known answer measure its error bars and its WARN factor (1.4 measured, 2 declared).

intro.text: Larmor is one small program. A Python engine (`nmr_twin/`) holds the twin and all the rules. A FastAPI server (`server.py`, `routes/`) exposes the engine as a JSON API. A plain JavaScript front end (`web/`) draws the pages. There is no database: the twin state is one JSON file (`state/twin_state.json`) with an append-only event log.

blocks.text: A scanner file becomes an evidence packet. The packet goes through a six-layer check. The check decides update, update with warning, or reject. Only checked evidence may move the twin, and how far it moves depends on how much the evidence can be trusted. The twin then predicts the next value and proposes the next measurement, which closes the loop back to the scanner.

blocks.text: The dossier (section 8.3) lists what a consumer must not assume. This is how the code enforces each one.

items: A number is not comparable across protocols. The checker compares sequence, TE, TR, field and frequency with the baseline and warns on any difference.
Passing QC does not make a biological reading certain. The verdict says "suggestive, not conclusive", and the explanations stay open.
A clean schema does not remove measurement bias. The schema is only layer 2 of 6; physics and metrology come after it.
A model prediction is not clinical truth. Every twin output is labelled INFERRED, and the page header says SIMULATED.
Engine: Python 3.11, numpy, scipy, jsonschema; scikit-image only for the 3D surfaces. No machine learning.
Server: FastAPI with uvicorn, one process, one lock around the twin.
Front end: vanilla JavaScript modules and hand-drawn SVG, no build step, fonts and icons served locally.
State: one JSON file plus an append-only event log. Any number on screen can be traced to its event.
Tests: pytest. They check the dossier's worked numbers, its cross-team checks and every practice packet.

blocks.text: Only the observation model and the state variables are specific to the brain. The evidence packet, the six-layer check, the uncertainty budget and the update rule stay the same for a battery cell seen by lithium MRI, an elastomer seal seen by single-sided NMR, or the scanner itself followed through its phantom record (dossier J.6).

Larmor is an educational prototype on synthetic data. It follows one synthetic brain, one frontal voxel and two sessions six months apart. It shows how evidence should move a belief; it says nothing about any real person. The drift it allows for, the warning factor and two failure limits are teaching assumptions or declared team policy, and they are marked as such. Outside the conditions listed below, the correct output is "not validated for this condition".
What the twin has been built and tested for. "Tested" means automatic tests on the StarterPack data and on our 19 practice packets.

header: What the code does outside it

blocks.text: Anything outside this table is "not validated for this condition". Today the checker warns on a protocol change and rejects unknown quantities. It does not yet refuse every out-of-domain packet in those words; that is listed under open items.

items: Every value in the app is of SIMULATED origin: synthetic spectra and images from the organizers' StarterPack v0.3.
The header of every page carries a SIMULATED badge. The engine adds the same disclaimer to the saved state.
A simulated value labelled MEASURED is rejected by the checker, so synthetic data cannot be passed off as real.
The twin does not diagnose, does not recommend treatment and does not predict risk for a person.
Its strongest statement is "suggestive, not conclusive". Insufficient evidence is an accepted outcome.
The next-measurement advice is about evidence (what to scan next), never about care.
This is an educational prototype. It is not a research tool and not a clinical system, and it is not a medical device.
Pseudonymous identifiers only: `sub-01`, `ses-baseline`, `ses-followup`. No names, birth dates or hospital numbers exist anywhere in the system.
The twin works in relative time (months since baseline). Session dates are used only to cross-check the packet's own relative time.
We never read DICOM headers. The code reads only NIfTI and NIfTI-MRS files and copies no DICOM identifiers into packets, state or logs.
The event log stores packet IDs, fingerprints and processing steps, not images.
Before any real health data: privacy, consent, governance and security review first, technical integration second (dossier Appendix I).
Bias is a measurement issue here. A model tuned on one scanner, field, protocol or population may not transfer.
Everything was built on one synthetic subject from one simulated scanner. We make no claim beyond the validation domain above.
Ratios to creatine assume creatine is stable. If creatine itself changes, the ratio is biased. We say this openly in the measurement card.
The quality limits (SNR 25, linewidth 10 Hz at 3 T) are field-specific. At low field they would need new values.

items: MEASURED: recorded by an instrument. Here the spectra are SIMULATED instead.
DERIVED: computed from data by a declared method. Example: the fitted Cho/Cr ratio.
INFERRED: a model statement about something not observed directly. Example: the twin state, its posterior interval and every update decision.
SIMULATED: produced by a forward model with known inputs. Example: every StarterPack file.

blocks.text: Every packet carries its origin and its label, and the twin data dictionary gives the label of every output field.

items: The team chose the question, the primary variable, the update policy and the limits, and answers for every claim.
Claude (Anthropic) was our coding tool. It wrote the code and the first drafts of these documents to our direction. Rehmoz Ayub directed and reviewed the work.
We did not take its output on trust. Every number the app shows is checked against the dossier by automatic tests, and the test bench grades the twin against known truth.
The help assistant inside the app runs on a local model on our own laptop. It answers only from our documents, and nothing leaves the machine.
No personal data were given to any AI. All inputs were the synthetic StarterPack and the dossier.
Refuse out-of-domain packets (other field, other voxel location) with the words "not validated for this condition", instead of only a warning.
Replace the teaching drift Q with test-retest data.
Repeat the WARN-factor measurement on real test-retest scans. Our test bench supports 1.4 on simulated scans, so the declared 2 is on the safe side there.
Agree the two proposed FAIL limits with the partners.
